comments.text_zh: tl;dr 看看 Svelte 的创作者做的这个精彩入门演讲：[VIDEO]，它涵盖了 Svelte 所解决的一些 React 的成长阵痛。虽然前端看起来像是在原地打转，但这些技术之间有着大大小小的差异，而且它们各自都引入了（至少对 JS 来说）新颖的东西……凭记忆随便说说（这个时间线可能不准确，但至少是我经历过的顺序）：- Backbone 让你摆脱 jQuery 面条式代码，帮助你真正管理数据和模型。它常与 Marionette 搭配来处理视图（眯眼一看，这就是组件的前身），并为应用的这一部分带来一些秩序。- Angular 打包了 Backbone 的数据处理（services）、Marionette 井然有序的视图分离（views、directives），但他们在 apply/digest 循环上犯了一个致命错误，而且可能鼓励了过多的复杂性。Angular 把所有东西都打包在一起，拥有一致的使用方式/文档/语义、熟悉的编程模式（MVC），以及 Google 这个大型企业赞助者，于是像野火一样流行起来。- Knockout 看到了 Angular 的 MVC，哀叹它的复杂性，并专注于 MVVM——简单地绑定模型，再加上一个相对简单的、按需响应式的控制器 - React 出现了，它提出了一个更简单的世界：唯一的一等公民是组件，其他一切都分开提供（这未必是新的，有一篇文章把它比作 Windows 的 COM 子系统）。React is alm
comments.text: tl;dr watch this fantastic intro to svelte talk by it's creator: [VIDEO] , it covers some of the growing pains of React that svelte addresses. While it might look like the frontend is going around in circles, there are major & minor differences between the technologies, and they have each introduced novel (to JS at least) things... Off the top of my head (this timeline might not be right but it's how I went through it at least): - Backbone got you away from jquery spaghetti, helped you actually manage your data & models. Often paired with Marionette to handle views (if you squint this is the precursor to components) and bring some order in that part of the app. - Angular bundles backbone's data handling (services), marionette's orderly view separation (views, directives), but they made a fatal mistake in the apply/digest cycle and maybe encouraging a bit too much complexity. Angular is everything bundled together, with consistent usage/documentation/semantics, a familiar programming pattern (MVC), and a large corporate sponsor in Google it caught on like wildfire. - Knockout sees Angular's MVC, laments it's complexity and focuses on MVVM -- simple binding of a model and a relatively simple reactive-where-necessary controller - React comes along and suggests an even simpler world where the only first class citizen is components and everything else comes separate (this isn't necessarily new, there is an article out there comparing it to COM subsystems for windows). React is alm

comments.story_title: The new wave of React state management
comments.why_zh: 创作者关于 Svelte 响应式方法的演讲
comments.quote_zh: 我强烈推荐听听创作者 Rich Harris 的这个演讲《Rethinking reactivity》
comments.text_zh: > 它是否解决了只重绘所需最小范围的问题（相对于普通 VDOM 方法）？是的，事实上我觉得想_不_只重绘最低限度反而挺难的 LOL。如果你想更了解 Svelte（哪怕你并不打算用它开发），我强烈推荐听听创作者 Rich Harris 的这个演讲《Rethinking reactivity》[VIDEO] > 但它是否解决了这样一个问题：当曾经使用某状态的组件已经不存在时，这些状态会不断增长且永远不会被 GC？我认为答案是肯定的。虽然我主要说的状态管理问题其实是单一事实来源（source of truth）问题。Svelte 提供全局 store 来存储数据，而存储在局部组件上的数据只是_变量_（没有 useState 或 hooks 之类复杂的东西），Svelte 编译器会处理一切。我现在还很关注的另一个东西是 SolidJS，它在前端开发上采用和 Svelte 非常相似的方法（用编译器而不是库），但提供的 API 对 React 开发者来说非常熟悉，所以学习曲线不大（当然 Svelte 的学习曲线也很平缓）。
comments.text: > Does it solve the problem of only redrawing the required minimum (beside the normal VDOM approach)? Yes, in fact I think it's actually pretty hard _not_ to redraw the bare minimum LOL. If you want to know more about Svelte (even if you're not looking to develop with it) I HIGHLY recommend listening to this presentation called "Rethinking reactivity" by Rich Harris (the creator) [VIDEO] > But does it solve the problem of growing state which never gets GC'd when components which used to use it are gone? I think the answer to the question is yes. Although the problem I'm speaking mostly about state management is the source of truth problem. Svelte provides a global store to store data, and data stored on local components are just _variables_ (no useState or hooks or anything complicated) where the Svelte compiler handles everything. Something else I'm really eyeing right now is SolidJS which takes a very similar approach to Svelte (compiler instead of library) for frontend development but provides an API that's very familiar to React developers so there's not much of a learning curve (although Svelte has a very easy learning curve too).

comments.text_zh: Svelte 很棒。Svelte 5 的 runes 尤其强大，因为它们让响应式能够突破组件边界。同一套响应式模型在任何地方都适用，无论你是在更新 DOM 还是编写普通应用逻辑。Rich Harris 指出，React 实际上并不是响应式的：“React 对你应用中流动的值没有任何理解。它不是响应式的。” Rich Harris - Rethinking reactivity: [VIDEO] > 现代 JavaScript 框架全都围绕响应式。改变应用状态，视图就会自动更新。但有个问题——在运行时跟踪状态变化会带来开销，这会挤占你的 bundle 大小和性能预算。在这次演讲中，我们将探索另一种方法：把响应式移进语言本身。你的应用即将变得比以往任何时候都更小、更快。他从电子表格这个原型级的响应式系统讲起。他把响应式定义为值根据依赖关系自动更新。并将其与 React 重新运行组件函数、对比虚拟 DOM 树的模型进行对照。他认为 React“不理解流经你应用的值”，因此它不是传统意义上的响应式。虚拟 DOM 纯属额外开销：[LINK] > 但事实证明，我们可以不用虚拟 DOM 就实现类似的编程模型——而这就是 Svelte 的用武之地。React 跟踪组件渲染；响应式系统跟踪数据依赖。React doe
comments.text: Svelte is awesome. Svelte 5's runes are especially powerful because they let reactivity escape the component boundary. The same reactive model works everywhere, whether you're updating the DOM or building plain application logic. Rich Harris makes the point that React isn't actually reactive: "React doesn’t have any understanding of the values running through your app. It is not Reactive." Rich Harris - Rethinking reactivity: [VIDEO] >Modern JavaScript frameworks are all about reactivity. Change your application's state, and the view updates automatically. But there's a catch — tracking state changes at runtime adds overhead that eats into your bundle size and performance budgets. In this talk, we'll discover an alternative approach: moving reactivity into the language itself. Your apps have never been smaller or faster than they're about to become. He starts with spreadsheets as the archetypal reactive system. Defines reactivity as values automatically updating according to dependency relationships. Contrasts that with React's model of rerunning component functions and diffing virtual DOM trees. Argues that React "doesn't understand the values flowing through your application" and therefore isn't reactive in the traditional sense. Virtual DOM is pure overhead: [LINK] >But it turns out that we can achieve a similar programming model without using virtual DOM — and that's where Svelte comes in. React tracks component renders; reactive systems track data dependencies. React doe

comments.author: rich_harris
comments.story_title: Svelte 3: Rethinking Reactivity
comments.why_zh: 与 SVG 性能相关的 Svelte 演示
comments.quote_zh: 你可能会喜欢这个演示
comments.text_zh: 我的看法是，复杂性就像能量一样，只能真正从一种形式转化为另一种形式。通常区分的是运行时复杂性和认知复杂性——手工优化命令式代码的结果。换句话说，就是开发者体验和用户体验之间经典的取舍。Svelte 的主张是，把它转化为构建时复杂性实际上才是唯一明智的做法。如果这意味着 DX 和 UX 不再相互冲突，那么 `npm run build` 中涉及多少复杂性其实并不重要。但回答你关于 SVG 的观点：Svelte 必须遵守与任何其他代码相同的基本约束，所以你最终仍会遇到性能问题（不过你可能会喜欢这个演示 [VIDEO]）。我目前正在探索的一个方向是，能否把同样的声明式/编译模型用作 WebGL API 的封装，不过现在还非常早期。
comments.text: My view on this is that complexity, like energy, can only really be converted from one form into another. Normally the distinction is between runtime complexity and cognitive complexity — the result of hand-optimised imperative code. In other words, the classic trade-off between developer experience and user experience. Svelte's claim is that converting it into build time complexity is in fact the only sensible thing to do. It doesn't really matter how much complexity is involved in `npm run build` if it means that DX and UX are no longer in tension. But to answer your point about SVG, Svelte has to obey the same fundamental constraints as any other code, so you will eventually hit performance issues (though you may enjoy this demo [VIDEO] ). One avenue I'm currently exploring is whether the same declarative/compiled model can be used as a wrapper around WebGL APIs, though it's very early days.

comments.author: ttfkam
comments.story_title: React: You Might Not Need an Effect
comments.text_zh: React 里没有任何东西我会觉得算“简洁”。也许它比过去需要的一堆样板代码稍微简洁一点，但我也就只能说到这。[VIDEO] 我们真该承认，下面这些全都是抽象泄漏，而不是 Web 开发整体上的固有好处：• shouldComponentUpdate • React.PureComponent • useMemo • useCallback • Concurrent mode。它们存在，完全是因为 React 的底层模型不够用，而我们开发者被迫用这一堆优化样板代码去干计算机该干的活。VDOM 正在死去。让它死吧。早就该往前走了。在现有基础上继续做任何 React 开发，都只是在沙子上继续盖楼。
comments.text: There is nothing in React I'd regard as "terse". Perhaps slightly more terse than the mountain of boilerplate it required previously, but that's as far as I'd go. [VIDEO] We really should accept that all of the following are ABSTRACTION LEAKS and not inherent benefits to web development at large: • shouldComponentUpdate • React.PureComponent • useMemo • useCallback • Concurrent mode They exist solely because React's underlying model is insufficient and we, the developers, are being made to do the computer's job with all this optimization boilerplate. The VDOM is dying. Let it die. It's long past time to move on. Any further React development in the existing foundation is just continuing to build upon sand.
